messages:
Maya (CSM): Hey team — Hydra dedicated bring-up scheduled Wed evening. Need final quota numbers, autoscale policy, and confirmation on fallback model. Jordan, any constraints from your side? :wave:
Jordan (Customer): Evening works after 18:00 PT. We need KMS + audit logs enabled before accepting traffic. Also flag: finance will do a pricing check next month.
Rahul (SRE): Proposed steady QPS: 140 qps. Peak warmup: 900 qps for 12m. Safety spike: 1800 qps for 30s to validate circuit breakers.
Sam (Solutions): We'll prepare a quantized small-model fallback (hydra-lite-q4) to route to if P95 token latency breaches 220ms for >90s. Also will add response truncation policy for very long prompts.
Maya (CSM): Jordan — noted finance check. Renewal risk: if costs exceed estimate by >15% we'll accelerate review. We'll capture acceptance criteria in the account playbook.
Jordan (Customer): Understood. Can we keep the main test outside our 810pm support window? That slot is peak for our clients.
Maya (CSM): We'll target 18:30 PT start then. Rahul, how long to rotate KMS and validate?
Rahul (SRE): KMS rotate is manual: create prod key in customer's KMS, update secrets, restart serving nodes. Estimated 1.5h plus QA. I'll open ticket and tag infra.
Sam (Solutions): Load plan: Phase A soak 140 qps for 45m. Phase B gradual ramp to 900 qps over 8m, hold 12m. Phase C safety spike 1800 qps for 30s. Measurements: p50/p95/p99, error %, token cost delta.
Rahul (SRE): Autoscale suggestion: min_replicas=3, max_replicas=50, scale_metric=requests_per_replica (target 30 r/s), combine with GPU_util >60% to scale further. Keep warm_pool=3. Cooldown 60s.
Sam (Solutions): Agree but lower cooldown to 30s for faster downscale after spikes. Add policy to pre-scale before scheduled spike (pre-warm job 10m prior).
Rahul (SRE): Fine with pre-warm. We'll also set fallback_policy: route >10% of traffic to hydra-lite-q4 when p95 >220ms for two consecutive windows (1m each).
Maya (CSM): ops-bot, please schedule canary and then full run at 18:30 PT Wed. Postmortem scheduled Thu 10am PT.
ops-bot: [automated] Canary scheduled for 18:15 PT. Will notify on any health anomalies.
Sam (Solutions): I'll post k6 scripts and the Jenkins job link in the runbook channel. Sample: `k6 run --vus 300 --duration 12m hydra_phaseB.js`
Maya (CSM): Jordan, can you confirm the blackout windows and who will sign off on post-test?
Jordan (Customer): Blackout 20:0022:00 PT. I'll sign off after reviewing the post-test summary with our engineering lead.
Rahul (SRE): Action items: (1) open KMS rotate ticket (ETA Mon); (2) provision reserved pool and warm_pool; (3) deploy autoscale policies and fallback routing; (4) assist during canary and load run.
Sam (Solutions): Action items: (1) upload load scripts and job; (2) prepare quantized model and rollback playbook; (3) capture token-level billing traces.
Maya (CSM): I'll update the account playbook with acceptance criteria: p95 <=120ms (steady), p95 <=220ms during spikes (with fallback), error-rate <0.2%, cost delta within quoted SLA. Renewal note: finance review in 6 weeks.
Jordan (Customer): Thanks. We'll have legal confirm KMS key rotation steps too.
ops-bot: [automated] Canary started. Health-checks ok: 12/12. Monitoring alert threshold set: 5% error-rate.
Maya (CSM): Great. Please post any blips in this thread. If anything slips, escalate to eng-oncall. :thumbsup:
Jordan (Customer): A few small asks after test: can reports include per-route latency and per-model token costs? We need that for our internal audit.
Sam (Solutions): Yes — we'll include per-route breakdown and cost-per-1k-token in the postmortem.
Rahul (SRE): Noted. Ticket numbers: KMS#12345 (rotation), POOL#6789 (provision). I'll update when done.
Maya (CSM): Closing checklist: KMS ticket, pool provisioned, scripts posted, canary run, full load, postmortem. Meeting Thu 10am PT for sign-off. Thanks everyone.
